metadata.case_name: LAU CHOK TING v. CHUN WO CONSTRUCTION AND ENGINEERING CO LTD AND OTHERS

injuries.description: Mild posterior prolapse (disc bulging) at L4/5 related to the accident
source: MRI scan showed degenerative changes of discs at L2 to S1 levels, with mild posterior prolapse (disc bulging) at L4/5, dural sac and nerve roots free from impeachment with mild posterior bulging of the disc at L5/S1.
the disc prolapse at L4-5 was related to acute trauma suffered during the accident.

source: MRI scan showed degenerative changes of discs at L2 to S1 levels, with mild posterior prolapse (disc bulging) at L4/5, dural sac and nerve roots free from impeachment with mild posterior bulging of the disc at L5/S1.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

source: After the accident the plaintiff went to the A&E Department of the Tuen Mun Hospital (“TMH”). He had low back pain. However the x-rays were normal and the doctors just diagnosed his injury as a back sprain. He was treated and discharged on the same day.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

manifestations.description: Tenderness over the left paraspinal muscles of his lower back
Constant pain with limitation to physical activities; reduced ability to jog and practise Tai Chi
Not fit to perform heavy physical jobs and requires assistance in lifting heavy objects; unable to return to pre-injury manual labour
No evidence of nerve root compression affecting his lower limbs (no neurological deficit found)

treatments_received: A&E treatment at Tuen Mun Hospital
treatments_future: medical consultations and treatments for back pain as required

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Before the accident the plaintiff enjoyed a variety of sports, in particular jogging and practising Tai Chi; since the accident his physical activities are limited to light exercises and Tai Chi with certain limitations.
The plaintiff could not return to his pre-injury job as manual labour/material handler and should take up lighter jobs; reduced employability in manual labour.
Reduced ability to perform vigorous physical work and lifting heavy objects; occasional inability to work full days.
